transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah… I’m here because flying has started to feel way scarier than it should. Like, even just thinking about getting on a plane, my mind goes right back to this really bad turbulence we had on my honeymoon flight. Which is silly, I know—people fly safely every day, and I tell myself that—but it still just… gets in my head.

Sorry, I was almost late today because I couldn’t find parking, and that kind of already had me wound up, but yeah, the main thing is the flying.
When did you first start feeling scared about flying?

I think it really started after that flight coming back from my honeymoon… the one with the awful turbulence. So, uh, about two years and five months ago now, I guess. Funny how I can remember that so clearly, but I’ll forget where I put my keys five minutes after walking in the door. But yeah—that’s when it started.
Has your fear of flying stopped you from taking any trips or traveling by air since your honeymoon?

Yeah… it has. I mean, I try to make it sound practical, like “oh, driving gives us more flexibility,” but really I’ve been choosing these ridiculously long drives instead of flying. And there have been a couple work trainings I just turned down because they would’ve meant getting on a plane.

Even just talking about planning a trip can make me want to back out, so if I absolutely have to deal with it, I kind of need my husband sitting there with me. Like, not doing anything dramatic, just being there so I don’t immediately say no.
Have you been avoiding other situations or activities because they might involve flying or lead to flying?

Yeah, mostly anything that could turn into “we should just fly there.” Like I’ll pick these really long drives instead, even when it’s kind of ridiculous. My husband jokes that I suddenly love road trips, but I don’t really—I mean, snacks are nice, I guess, but that’s not the reason.

And with work, there were trainings I turned down because they involved flying. I didn’t make a big announcement about it or anything, I just found reasons not to go. If we have to talk about a trip, I kind of need my husband sitting with me, because otherwise I’ll start trying to back out before we even get anywhere with the planning.
How much distress or anxiety do you feel when you think about flying or are in a situation where you might have to fly?

It’s pretty immediate, honestly. Like if I’m looking up flights for a conference—sometimes I’ll tell myself I’m just checking prices, nothing serious—but my chest tightens right away and I get this rush of panic, like I need to shut the laptop.

Even hearing a plane go overhead can do it sometimes, which is annoying because we’re not even that close to the airport… though my neighbor swears the flight paths changed, I don’t know. But yeah, it’s like my body reacts before I’ve even really thought it through, and I just want to get away from the whole idea.
Has your fear of flying affected your relationships with family or friends in any way?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m not falling apart or anything — I still go to work, I still handle things at home — but it’s starting to mess with plans more than I’d like.

Like, with my supervisor, she’s mentioned these trainings and conferences that would probably be good for me, and I’ve kind of… passed on them. I make it sound like scheduling, or budget, or whatever, but really it’s the flying part.

And personally, too. My husband and I had talked about this Florence trip I was really excited about — I even saved restaurants on my phone, which is silly because I don’t even know when we’d go — but it just keeps getting pushed back. So I guess it affects him too, because he’s patient about it, but I know it changes what we can actually plan.
Is your fear of flying the main thing that's causing you distress, or are there other things that worry you just as much or more?

I think it’s mostly the flying, yeah. I mean, I worry about normal stuff too—work things, whether I remembered to buy laundry detergent, all that boring life stuff—but this is the thing that feels… bigger than it should.

Like just imagining getting on a plane, I’m right back to that honeymoon flight where there was all that turbulence. And I know, logically, people fly every day and they’re fine. My husband says that too, and I’ll nod like, yes, obviously, I understand statistics. But then my brain just kind of ignores that and goes straight to picturing the plane dropping again.

So, yeah, the flying is the main thing I’m here about.
Are there any other situations or things that trigger anxiety for you, aside from flying?

Not really that I can think of. I mean, I get stressed about things like anybody does—work can be a lot, especially when parents are upset about something that honestly has nothing to do with me, like parking at pickup time—but it’s not the same feeling.

I’m trying to think if there’s anything else that gives me that kind of immediate reaction… and no, I don’t think so. It’s mostly the flying thing.
Do you think your fear of flying is something that you could overcome if you really had to, or does it feel like it's a part of who you are now?

I don’t know… I’d like to think I could overcome it if I really had to. I’m not someone who wants to be, like, “Well, this is just me forever,” you know?

But then I think about actually doing it, like buying the ticket and going through security and sitting there waiting to board, and it starts to feel less simple. It’s funny, because I can handle a lot of other stressful things — at work there are days where three people need something from me at once and a kid has lost their backpack and someone’s upset about forms — and I can just deal with it. But flying feels like this one weird wall.

So… I guess I don’t think it’s part of who I am, exactly. I think I could maybe get past it, but right now it definitely feels bigger than just “push through it.”
Has your fear of flying affected your daily routine or activities in any significant way?

I mean, day to day, I’m still functioning. I go to work, I keep up with stuff at home, laundry still gets done eventually—well, most of the time. My husband would probably say the mail pile is its own separate issue, but that’s not really the flying thing.

It’s more that I’ve started saying no to things I probably shouldn’t. Like trainings or conferences my supervisor thinks would be good for me, career-wise. If they’re out of town and flying is involved, I just kind of find a reason not to go. And personally, we keep pushing back this Florence trip I was really excited about, which makes me feel ridiculous because I used to look at pictures of the museums and food and all that, and now I just get stuck on the plane part.

So it hasn’t wrecked my daily routine, but it is definitely limiting things.
Do you experience any physical symptoms, like a racing heart or sweating, when you think about flying?

Yeah, I do. It’s pretty immediate, actually. Like if I’m looking up flights for a conference or something, my chest gets tight right away, and I get this rush of panic where I just want to close the laptop.

Even hearing a plane overhead can kind of set it off for a second, which is embarrassing because obviously it’s just a plane going by. My husband will be talking about something totally unrelated, like what we’re doing for dinner or whether we need more laundry detergent, and then I hear it and my brain just jumps there. It’s not like I’m trying to think about it—it just happens, and I want to get away from the thought.
Have you had to take time off work or school due to your fear of flying?

Not really in the sense of calling out sick or taking a day off because of it. I still go to work, I still do my normal stuff.

It’s more like… I avoid work things that would involve flying. My supervisor has brought up trainings and conferences that would probably be good for me, and I sort of find reasons not to go if I’d have to fly. Which is awkward, because then I’m acting like it’s a scheduling thing or a budget thing, when really it’s the plane.

And then at home, it’s the same kind of thing with trips. We’ve been putting off this Florence trip I was really excited about—my husband keeps joking that by the time we go, we’ll have watched every travel video online. So no, I haven’t taken time off exactly, but it definitely gets in the way.
Has your fear of flying caused any problems in your relationships with friends?

With friends? Not too much, I don’t think. I mean, nobody’s stopped talking to me over it or anything like that.

It’s more that I probably seem flaky sometimes, because if someone mentions a destination wedding or a girls’ trip that would mean flying, I kind of… change the subject or say I’m busy. And then I feel bad, because it’s not really about them.

Honestly, the bigger stuff has been work and home plans—like I’m still managing my job and everything, but I’ve skipped out on trainings or conferences my supervisor thought would be good for me. And my husband and I keep pushing back this Florence trip I was really excited about. So with friends it’s maybe awkward here and there, but it hasn’t caused a huge fight or anything.
Are you avoiding social gatherings or events because they might involve flying or talking about flying?

Yeah… sort of. I mean, not like I’m avoiding every social event, but if something involves flying, I’ll usually start looking for a way around it. Like I’ve chosen really long drives before instead of just getting on a plane, even when it made the trip kind of ridiculous.

And with work trainings, if they’re far enough that I’d have to fly, I’ve definitely turned them down or made it sound like the timing wasn’t great. Which… I don’t love admitting.

If it’s just talking about a trip, I can sometimes do it, but I usually need my husband sitting there with me, because otherwise I’ll start backing out or shut the whole conversation down. He’s gotten weirdly good at keeping me on track—like, “Okay, just look at the dates, don’t close the laptop.”
Have you ever had a panic attack related to your fear of flying?

I don’t know if I’d call it a full panic attack, exactly… I always picture that as something really dramatic. But I do get this immediate rush of panic.

Like if I’m looking up flights for a work conference, my chest tightens right away and I just want to shut the laptop. Or even sometimes if I hear a plane overhead, I’ll suddenly get that feeling like I need to get away from the thought, if that makes sense.

It’s annoying because it can be something totally ordinary—I could be making dinner or answering emails—and then there’s a plane sound, and my brain just goes, “Nope.”
